lines.text: The giant woke once. Now the mountains themselves are stirring. In the legends of Germany, an emperor sleeps beneath the peaks — and above them walks Rübezahl, the lord of the mountains.
And in the forests of Paraguay, the Pombéro keeps watch one last time. Tonight, in the last thirty-two, the mountain meets the night again.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode seventy-nine. Germany, versus Paraguay. A knockout. There is no way back.
Germany arrive as four-time world champions, and this time the machine is fully awake. Paraguay arrive as Los Guaraníes — unbowed, unafraid, and dreaming of the shock of the tournament.
Germany — Die Mannschaft. Precise, patient, ruthless. A nation that has turned winning into an engineering problem.
Florian Wirtz pulls the strings, the heartbeat of the new Germany. Jamal Musiala dances through defences as if gravity forgot him. And Kai Havertz leads the line, all elegance and danger.
Joshua Kimmich, the captain, conducts from deep. And Antonio Rüdiger marshals a back line that gives away nothing.
Paraguay — Los Guaraníes. Iron in defence, fire in the heart, a team built on grit and the memory of every doubter who wrote them off.
Gustavo Gómez, the captain — the wall the whole nation leans on. Miguel Almirón, electric on the break. Julio Enciso, the spark who can light a night from nothing.
Diego Gómez drives the midfield with fearless energy. And Antonio Sanabria leads the line, hunting the one chance that could shock the world.
So here is the riddle. Can the wall hold for ninety minutes against a machine that has finally found its rhythm? Or does the night steal one more miracle?
And stay with me — because this one is settled late, with two strokes of pure German class.
Here is how we see it. Paraguay defend like men possessed — bodies thrown in front of everything, the keeper a wall of his own.
For an hour the wall holds. The machine probes, and passes, and waits.
And Paraguay almost steal it — Enciso breaks and drives at goal, a shot that screams just past the post. Inches from the upset of the tournament.
But the mountain does not crack. And then, at last, it moves. Gómez throws his body into one more heroic block — but only one.
The seventy-eighth minute. Florian Wirtz glides through and finishes, cool as ice. One — nil. The mountain wakes.
And then the killer blow. The eighty-eighth minute. Kai Havertz rises and heads it home. Two — nil. The machine marches on.
Two goals in ten minutes. Ninety minutes of resistance, undone by a team that simply would not be denied. Cruel — and somehow inevitable.
Our prediction — Germany two, Paraguay nil. Wirtz and Havertz, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And the Guaraníes leave with their heads high — because they made a four-time champion sweat for every single inch of the night.
Germany march on. But Paraguay reminded the world that a nation written off can still make the favourites tremble until the very last breath.
So you tell me — the mountain, or the night? Comment GERMANY for Die Mannschaft — comment PARAGUAY for Los Guaraníes.

High on the storm-wreathed peaks of Germany, they speak of Rübezahl — the lord of the mountains, ancient and vast, who tests every traveller, humbles the arrogant, and rewards the humble and the brave. Legend seventy-nine — Rübezahl, Lord of the Mountains.
The players write the night. Rübezahl carries one truth — the mountain belongs to no one. It is only ever borrowed by those bold enough to climb it.
Here is how. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds, and Rübezahl, Legend seventy-nine, unlocks the moment you sign up.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for fun. No prizes — only glory.
So sign up tonight, claim your Legend, and send this to someone who never stops climbing. Hit like, subscribe — and I'll see you when the next legend steps from the mist.
